name: McLaren M6 GT
description:
The McLaren M6 GT is one of the rarest and most significant cars in McLaren's history, representing Bruce McLaren's ambitious attempt to create a road-legal supercar from his successful Can-Am racing program. Only three examples were ever completed before Bruce McLaren's tragic death in 1970 brought the project to an end.

Based on the dominant M6A Can-Am car, the M6 GT featured a modified chassis with a longer wheelbase and an enclosed coupe body designed for road use. The aluminum monocoque construction kept weight to approximately 800 kg despite the addition of road-going amenities. Power came from a Chevrolet small-block V8, bored and stroked to produce around 500 horsepower at 7,000 RPM.

Bruce McLaren personally used one of the three M6 GTs as his daily driver, commuting between his home and the McLaren factory. This remarkable fact speaks to both the car's practicality and McLaren's confidence in his engineering. The car combined genuine racing performance with surprising road manners.

The M6 GT project demonstrated McLaren's vision of becoming a manufacturer of high-performance road cars, a dream that would not be fully realized until the F1 supercar arrived over two decades later. Today, the M6 GT stands as a poignant reminder of what might have been, and as a direct spiritual ancestor to every McLaren road car that followed.
